title: Lope Hurtado de Mendoza (Rome) to Charles V, May 1523 - Mar 1524 - RAH Salazar 9/28 and 9/30, DECODE R9667-R9869

steps.what: Grepped Bergenroth CSP Spain vol. 2 (1523-24 sections, british-history.ac.uk) for each record's Salazar folio. R9667 = no. 548 (A.28 ff. 6-9, 5 May 1523, 'Autograph in cipher. Contemporary deciphering'); R9846 = no. 617 (A.30 ff. 130-133, 5 Feb 1524). Other six folios not calendared.

Fetched the 8 DECODE records and 17 images. Dates read off the documents: R9695 is 8 July 1523, not June; four records are Feb-Mar 1524 (Salazar A-30), not 1523; two are addressed to a "muy Illustre senor", not the Emperor.
Same cipher as the 1522 Hurtado letters (targets/lopehurtado/): the code groups ton, zar, xul, rab, taf, yub, teg, xug recur on every leaf.
Found two bound-in contemporary clears: R9667 f. 9v 'Claro' leaf for sections A and B, and R9846 f. 133r clear version of a letter almost wholly in cipher.

Tried R9667's bound 'Claro' leaf as a crib: it is mirrored and docketed 'Del abbad de Najera a dos de mayo', so it belongs to another letter. Transcribed the six cipher runs; codes only give fragments (a request for benefices for the Pope's servants); 4ʃL∂8ɛ probable 'provea'.

Aligned R9846 ff. 130r-130v cipher (38 lines) against the contemporary clear on f. 133r, clause for clause. 105 values (65 confirmed, 40 probable) in key_1524.tsv; most of the homophonic letter alphabet recovered from exact-count spelled runs; 1522 letter values 4=n, 8=e, 7=a, m=o re-confirmed; 25 1522 codes re-confirmed. Contradictions: L sits as r (1522: i), tef in a 'nec-' slot (1522: paz).

Applied key_1524 to R9683, R9695, R9867 (no crib). R9867 (all cipher) dated by its own spelled date line: Rome, 4 Jan 1524; frame reads (Beaurain, money), ~30 code groups unknown. R9683 (10 June 1523) and R9695 (8 July 1523, draft) cipher runs yield fragments only. New probable: 3=h, tuf=Roma.

Applied the key to R9869, R9866, R9868. Dates fixed from subscriptions: 28 Mar, 28 Feb, 20 Mar 1524; R9866 and R9868 to Gattinara. R9869 ~2/3 reads, R9868 f.430r mostly, R9866 a quarter to a third. New: barred m = f (confirmed), tef = nec- confirmed three times (1522: paz).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2868 tokens, 150 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.148 per letter; random keys -3.719 (z 6.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.509 (mean -2.517, z 29.4); annealer on the real text -2.196. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): eight records: cipher files r96*/r98*_cipher.txt; transcriptions of R9866/R9868/R9869 copied from their read_*.md to texts/; decryptions read_*.md, R9846 clear + alignment, R9667 alignment + retry; key_1524*.tsv, key_1523*.tsv, key_merged.tsv, key_retry.tsv.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). read_r*.md, r9667_alignment.md and retry_2026-09-21.md read: in every letter but R9846 the clear text reads and the cipher runs give word pieces with […] gaps in nearly every clause (R9667: five of six runs unread; R9683: 'cipher mostly unread'; R9867: gaps in every clause). Seven letters relabelled decoded, not read. R9846's transcribed cipher is covered clause for clause by the clerk's clear on f. 133r, which reads (reading_review A). Method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> read from existing decipherment (parts); fraction_read 0.45 -> ~0.23 (estimated).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b07). Existing text sought: no contemporary decipherment on any DECODE image of the seven unread letters (CSP Spain ii 548 says R9667 had one, not imaged); CSP calendars only R9667 and R9846; web search 22 Oct found nothing. The RAH Biblioteca Digital answers only through an Anubis proof-of-work bot check, not passed, so better images of Salazar A-28/A-30 were not checked.

Every cipher run of R9866, R9867, R9868, R9869, R9683 and R9667 re-read on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images (b07_crop.py), and the f. 444v clear of R9869 transcribed in full. Look-alikes resolved word by word (<doc>_corrections.tsv): the ß-like a was transcribed ʇʇ (r) in a dozen words; y ʇʇ is one sign ɣ̶ (g: coligados, enemigos, colegio, alargar); m̶ is f or c, ʒ is p; xab -> rab, ʒul -> zul, zaf -> yaf, y m̶ -> ym (fue) in R9869.

Code groups from new contexts (probable, key files unchanged): zm = como (R9867 l21, R9866 R14), ʃeg = tengo (R9866 R14 "como tengo escrito", R9869 R7), zub = alla (1522 value; R9866 R5 "la costa de alla", R9867 l23), zad probably a look-alike of zed = arçobispo (R9868 R7 after the clear "partida del señor arçobispo de Capua"). In R9683/R9667 the 1522 sign values & = o, H = e, ɭb = p, ∠ = v give "Theodorico", "servi[ci]o", "pensava", "declare", "era del que mas se".

Readings built sentence by sentence (<doc>_reading.md, English <doc>_en.md) and aligned word by word with the decodes (words fixed: R9869 bueno -> [?bueno], R9868 a -> [?a], R9866 como/tiene -> [?…]). Clean share of the reading bodies (b07_score.py): R9866 0.667, R9868 0.638, R9869 0.622 (read, grade B); R9867 0.389 (decoded, not read); R9683 0.636 and R9667 0.767 on the whole letter but kept decoded, not read because their cipher passages do not build sentences; R9695 not attempted further. English for R9846 (read since the audit) written: R9846_en.md.

Consistency pass (cl): outcome.texts summary reworded for docs/_check_terms.py (outcome words 'read', 'undeciphered', 'unsolved' replaced by what happened: deciphered, given a value, transcribed, no decipherment known); facts unchanged.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 2 of 4 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.148; polyphony 0.0; 198 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.196

Key rebuilt from R9846's bound clear; on 22 Oct 2026 three 1524 letters (R9866, R9868, R9869) read with it after a sign-by-sign re-read on the images; R9867 and the three 1523 letters stay decoded, not read (open codes, 1523 sign set unkeyed, R9667's decipherment not imaged).

outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, re-read batch b07: cipher tokens of the documents that read / all, counted by decode_merged.py over the transcriptions (R9667 152, R9683 91, R9695 249, R9846 764, R9866 624, R9867 467, R9868 353, R9869 339 = 3,039) plus R9846's untranscribed ff. 131-132 (124, from the notes' count of 888): read R9846 ff. 130r-v 764 + R9866 624 + R9868 353 + R9869 339 = 2,080 / 3,163 = 0.66 (estimated: R9846's untranscribed share and the 1523 counts come from different transcriptions). Before: 0.23 (reading audit, R9846 only). The 0.66 is a share of cipher tokens in the letters that read, not a count of tokens each given a value: the readings themselves score 0.667 (R9866), 0.638 (R9868) and 0.622 (R9869) clean sentences, and 0.45 was withdrawn as a reading figure (NOTES.md, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R9667, Rome, 5 May 1523, to Charles V (9/28 ff. 6-9)
texts.summary: Clear letter with cipher runs on the Pope's servants and the benefices the Pope wants for them; CSP Spain ii no. 548 abstracts it from a lost contemporary decipherment (the Pope has not yet declared his alliance, the French have lost hope, Theodorico was most suspected). Only fragments of the cipher runs are deciphered; the 'Claro' leaf beside it is the Abbot of Nájera's clear of 2 May 1523, not Hurtado's.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b07; R9667_reading.md, R9667_en.md, R9667-R9869_reread_log.md): the clear text reads (whole-letter share 0.767), but of the six cipher runs only C ("que era del que mas se [?sospechava]", with CSP 548's topic) and pieces of A ("el papa no se declare") and B ("[?franceses] que [?pensava]") read. The contemporary decipherment CSP Spain ii 548 was made from is not on the DECODE images. Blockers: open-codes (1523 sign set unkeyed) and needs-physical-access (RAH Salazar A-28).

texts.label: R9683, Rome, June 1523, to Charles V (9/28 f. 171)
texts.summary: The Duke of Sessa's letters report the Pope's good will after the arrest of Cardinal Soderini of Volterra; the Emperor should restore the benefices of the chamberlain Pedro and Francisco and pay the Pope what is owed him. Most of the cipher passages are not deciphered.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b07; R9683_reading.md, R9683_en.md, R9667-R9869_reread_log.md): the clear text reads and the whole-letter share is 0.636, but the cipher passage does not: only "de [?Theodorico] que sol[o] el …", "el [?duque] esta bienquisto de Su Sd. … para con su [?servicio]" and "para que la [?cruzada] …" hold. The 1523 hand uses letter signs of the 1522 notation not in the 1524 key, and there is no 1523 crib. Blocker: open-codes.

texts.label: R9695, Rome, 8 July 1523, autograph draft to Charles V (9/28 ff. 339-340)
texts.summary: The Pope was pleased with the Emperor's letter; the rumoured poisoning could not be verified, the Pope guards his person and eats apart, and Hurtado asks for naturalisations for the Pope's intimates (Pedro de Roma, Francisco, Theodorico). The clear text is transcribed in part; the cipher lines are not deciphered.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b07; R9667-R9869_reread_log.md): not attempted further on 22 Oct 2026 (batch b07): autograph draft with struck cipher lines in the 1523 sign set, clear transcription incomplete; same blocker as R9683/R9667 (open-codes, no 1523 crib).

texts.label: R9846, Rome, 3 and 5 Feb 1524, to Charles V (9/30 ff. 130-133)
texts.summary: The Pope is glad of the coming of Monsieur de Beaurain; on the contribution, money is short and every help is needed; the Pope wants France ruined or a truce (CSP Spain ii no. 617). The first third is deciphered by aligning the cipher with the clerk's clear on f. 133r; the rest of the clear (f. 133v) is not imaged.

reading_review.note: The transcribed cipher (ff. 130r-v, c05-v17, 768 tokens) is covered clause for clause by the clerk's contemporary clear on f. 133r (r9846_clear.txt), which reads as continuous Spanish; the alignment (r9846_alignment.md) confirms the match. The score is low from the diplomatic line-by-line layout and abbreviations.

texts.note: Clear text with cipher runs: the clear reads, but the cipher runs decode only into word pieces and single letters, with unknown code groups in nearly every clause ('que sol[o] el […] esta mas […] para […]'); no cipher sentence can be built (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R9866, Rome, 28 Feb 1524, to Grand Chancellor Gattinara (9/30 ff. 285-286)
texts.summary: To Gattinara: Beaurain's coming was timely; the French mean, by craft or force, to stay on this side of the Alps, and the Emperor must not lose the world's respect while he spends so much on the war; Hurtado asks Gattinara's help to be paid what he is owed. Read a quarter to a third.

reading_review.note: Clean share 0.667 (b07_score.py, reading body). The French mean to stay this side of the Alps; the Emperor must not grant peace or truce while they hold a palm of ground, must drive them out ("si no son vencidos, quedan vencedores"), and should have Naples pay the army; Beaurain will report. Holes: the codes xer, tas, yab, tol-type groups, R3 "[?] por pocos", R9 opening, R14 middle. Rests on the clear text checked on the full-resolution DECODE images and the cipher runs decoded with the merged 1523-24 key (key_merged.tsv, rebuilt from R9846's f. 133r clear), every run re-read sign by sign on the images with the look-alike signs resolved word by word (R9866_corrections.tsv: the ß-like a transcribed as ʇʇ, y ʇʇ = ɣ̶ g, m̶ = f or c, ʒ = p); aligned word by word with the decode, supplied words bracketed. No contemporary decipherment, clear copy or edition exists. Log: R9667-R9869_reread_log.md.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 91.4% of the words of R9866_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: R9867, Rome, 4 Jan 1524, to Charles V (9/30 f. 351)
texts.summary: Wholly in cipher: Monsieur de Beaurain has left the Pope content with what he said on the Emperor's behalf; the Emperor must not show need of money, little can be raised; mention of the archbishop [of Capua] and the French in Italy; the writer asks for what is owed to him.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b07; R9867_reading.md, R9867_en.md, R9667-R9869_reread_log.md): clean share 0.389 (wholly cipher): Beaurain leaves the Pope content; the Emperor must not show need of money; if the French stay in Italy …; Hurtado will do as ordered and asks to be paid what is owed him "alla"; but about half the sentences break on open codes (rub, ʃug, tol, xer, xal, xir, ʃal, co, ℮, ʃφ). Blocker: open-codes, no crib.

texts.label: R9868, Rome, 20 Mar 1524, to Grand Chancellor Gattinara (9/30 ff. 430-431)
texts.summary: Hurtado sends Gattinara a copy of his 11 March letter: the archbishop of Capua has left and all business hangs on the Datary [Giberti], who must be satisfied; benefices shared among the Cardinals; the Pope's servants should be rewarded and many Cardinals want to be Protector.

reading_review.note: Clean share 0.638. The Datary must be rewarded; the archbishop of Capua's absence will not help; the Pope's servants who stayed are very mistrustful; naturalisations for two or three closest to the Pope; the protectorship better with Colonna, whom Vespasiano obeys as he did his father Prospero; he could complain with cause if forgotten. Holes: zid, ʃug, yic, toc, R14, the last word of R13. Rests on the clear text checked on the full-resolution DECODE images and the cipher runs decoded with the merged 1523-24 key (key_merged.tsv, rebuilt from R9846's f. 133r clear), every run re-read sign by sign on the images with the look-alike signs resolved word by word (R9868_corrections.tsv: the ß-like a transcribed as ʇʇ, y ʇʇ = ɣ̶ g, m̶ = f or c, ʒ = p); aligned word by word with the decode, supplied words bracketed. No contemporary decipherment, clear copy or edition exists. Log: R9667-R9869_reread_log.md.

texts.label: R9869, Rome, 28 Mar 1524, to Charles V (9/30 ff. 444-445)
texts.summary: The money the Pope offered through Beaurain; Florence has taken no decision; Cardinal Cortona and Ippolito de' Medici leave for Florence; the archbishop of Capua should be well received by the Emperor; the Pope's goodwill and words could not be better. The rest (Easter news, Hungary and the Turk, the Infante) is in clear.

reading_review.note: Clean share 0.622. The Pope will fulfil the rest of the money offered to Beaurain but pleads need; Florence undecided; if the archbishop finds the army ready, the Pope's deeds will match what he offered when elected; any help with money is good; the clear (f. 444v transcribed in full): Easter news of Hungary and the Turk, the Legate at Nuremberg, too few letters from the Emperor. Holes: R1 (what Beaurain was sent), R5, parts of R9-R11. Rests on the clear text checked on the full-resolution DECODE images and the cipher runs decoded with the merged 1523-24 key (key_merged.tsv, rebuilt from R9846's f. 133r clear), every run re-read sign by sign on the images with the look-alike signs resolved word by word (R9869_corrections.tsv: the ß-like a transcribed as ʇʇ, y ʇʇ = ɣ̶ g, m̶ = f or c, ʒ = p); aligned word by word with the decode, supplied words bracketed. No contemporary decipherment, clear copy or edition exists. Log: R9667-R9869_reread_log.md.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 92.7% of the words of R9869_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

parts.label: R9846, ff. 130r-v (clerk's clear on f. 133r)
parts.basis: the contemporary clear of the first part of the 5 Feb 1524 letter, bound as f. 133r and aligned clause for clause (r9846_clear.txt, r9846_alignment.md); ff. 131-132 and the rest of the clear (f. 133v, not imaged) are open

parts.label: R9667, R9683, R9695, R9867 (decoded, not read)
parts.basis: R9867 (wholly cipher) breaks on about fifteen open codes; the three 1523 letters use letter signs of the 1522 notation not in the 1524 key and have no crib, and R9667's contemporary decipherment (CSP Spain ii 548) is not imaged. Their clear text reads.

prior.where: Bergenroth, CSP Spain vol. 2 (1866) nos. 548 (R9667) and 617 (R9846) abstract two of the letters from their contemporary decipherments; the other six are not calendared. No modern decipherment found.
